after: ## Assignment: evaluate on the right, store on the left
alt: The statement a = a * b; with the right side marked "evaluate first" and the left variable marked "store here". Before, a holds 3 and b holds 5; the right side 3 * 5 evaluates to the int 15; after, a holds 15 and b still holds 5.
caption: The right side is evaluated with the current values, then the result replaces the left variable.

after: ## Assignment: evaluate on the right, store on the left
alt: A four-line Java segment and its trace table. a is set to 3, b to a + 2 = 5, then a becomes a * b = 15, and finally b becomes b - a = 5 - 15 = -10, so the program prints 15 -10. In each row only the left-hand variable changes.
caption: One row per statement, and each statement changes only the variable on its left.

after: ### An expression has a value and a type
alt: A grid of value types against variable types. An int value can be stored in an int or a double variable, where 5 becomes 5.0; a double value only in a double variable, even if it looks whole; a boolean value only in a boolean variable. Below: double d = a + 2; compiles, int n = 2.5 * 2; does not.
caption: The compiler checks the type of the value, not whether it looks like a whole number.

after: ### Initialization: a variable must have a value before it is used
alt: Top: int y; declares y with no value, so int z = y + 1; fails with "variable y might not have been initialized". Bottom: the String variable title holds an arrow to a String object "Dune", while empty holds null and refers to no object; primitives cannot hold null, and "" is a real empty String.
caption: A variable must be given a value before use, and null means no object at all.

after: ## Input: getting values from a user
alt: Three lines of keyboard input, "Ada Lovelace", 36 and 1.65, each followed by an end-of-line marker. Each Scanner call reads one item and its value is assigned to a variable: name holds "Ada Lovelace", age holds 36 and height holds 1.65. A table lists nextInt, nextDouble, nextBoolean, next and nextLine.
caption: Each Scanner call is an expression whose value is stored by an assignment.

alt: The input 5, end-of-line, hello, end-of-line, with a read position marker. nextInt() reads 5 and stops before the end-of-line. The first nextLine() reads the empty rest of that line, so rest is the empty string. The second nextLine() reads hello. The program prints [] then [hello].
caption: nextInt() leaves the end-of-line behind, so the next nextLine() returns an empty string.

after: ## A reliable method for tracing assignments
alt: Four tracing moves: a column per variable with its type, one statement at a time, right side first, overwrite only the left. Applied to worked example 1, items goes 4 then 5, price goes 2.5 then 5.0, and cost goes 10.0 then 22.5, so the program prints 5 5.0 22.5.
caption: Columns, one row per statement, right side first: the output is 5 5.0 22.5.

after: ## Worked example 2: A program driven by input
alt: Flowchart of the rectangle program. Two input steps read 4.5 into length and 3 into width as 3.0; area = length * width gives 13.5; perimeter = 2 * (length + width) evaluates the bracket to 7.5 then gives 15.0; the program prints Area: 13.5 and Perimeter: 15.0.
caption: Read, compute, print: every variable is assigned before it is used.
